title: FilterInvalidInputImages
description: Required structured output for a Sonnet 5 VLM agent that names the Class 7/8 truck type in a photo, or rejects the photo as invalid input. On every call, return reasoning first, then output. The only allowed truck_type values are day-cab-truck, dump-truck, sleeper-truck, and none. Validity is exactly whether truck_type is not none. Decide TYPE from the vehicle's BODY AND CAB LAYOUT, not from generic heavy-truck hardware. First ask: is a dump body, a sleeper box/bunk, or a day-cab tractor layout actually visible? If yes, pick that type. If the crop is only a shared part (engine, dash, one wheel, a tank, a frame rail) and no layout is visible, do not guess dump or sleeper -- and do not treat that shared part as proof of a day-cab either unless a Class 7/8 tractor cab or fifth-wheel is also in frame. Class 7/8 means GVWR 26,001 lb and up: highway tractors and heavy vocational dumps. Class 2–6 means pickups and Super Duty chassis-cabs, cargo vans, step vans, cutaway cube trucks, moving and cargo straight box trucks, medium stake and flatbed trucks, and service/utility bodies on a pickup or medium chassis. Rule 1 (DAY-CAB-TRUCK -- HOW IT LOOKS): a Class 7/8 highway tractor whose cab STOPS at a flat rear wall right behind the seats. On a side or three-quarter view you see a tall tractor cab, a long conventional hood, West Coast mirrors, and then OPEN FRAME to a fifth-wheel plate -- no bunk box, no raised sleeper roof, no dump bed. The cab rear is a short vertical wall, not a hotel-room box. Typical brands in this role are Freightliner Cascadia day cab, International LT/ProStar day cab, Peterbilt/Kenworth/Mack/Volvo/Western Star day cabs. A day-cab close-up is valid only when it still shows that tractor cab or fifth-wheel layout. Rule 2 (DUMP-TRUCK -- HOW IT LOOKS): a Class 7/8 vocational truck whose cargo body is an OPEN-TOP DUMP, hopper, or grain box that tips. Look for ribbed steel/aluminum dump sides, a swinging or high-lift tailgate with chains or latches, a hydraulic hoist cylinder or doghouse, a tarp roller across the front of the bed, an open cargo volume with aggregate residue, and often a tandem or tridem axle group under that bed. The cab may be a day cab, but the BODY is a dump -- type the body. A rear-only dump tailgate or a shot from inside the dump bed still counts. A lift axle, air bag, or hydraulic ram by itself is NOT a dump body. Rule 3 (SLEEPER-TRUCK -- HOW IT LOOKS): a Class 7/8 highway tractor with a SLEEPER COMPARTMENT behind the seats. On the exterior that is a raised or extended box faired into the cab, often with its own side window, vent, or roof fairing, making the cab much longer than a day cab. On the interior that is a bunk mattress, overhead cabinet, netted shelf, sleeper curtain, or the walk-back living space behind the seats. A tractor cab interior that only shows seats and dash, with no bunk or sleeper wall, is not enough to call sleeper-truck. Rule 4 (NONE -- HOW INVALID INPUT LOOKS): pickups and Super Duty / F-450 / F-550 / Ram / Silverado chassis-cabs, including their beds, crew-cab interiors, and door badges; cargo vans (Express, Transit, Promaster); step vans / walk-in parcel bodies; cutaway cube vans; moving and cargo STRAIGHT BOX trucks -- an enclosed dry-freight or moving van body with roll-up or barn doors and often a liftgate is none, even if the box is large; medium-duty conventionals that carry a box (Freightliner M2 / Business Class, International 4000 / DuraStar / MV, Ford F-650/F-750) are none; wood-plank stake and short medium flatbeds on a single rear axle; service/utility/mechanic bodies on a pickup chassis; empty cargo-box interiors (E-track, plywood, roll-up door); a door-jamb sticker with printed GVWR under 26,001 lb; cars, SUVs, equipment, or scenery. Rule 5 (AN ENCLOSED BOX IS none): a cube, dry van, moving box, or liftgate-only rear view is none. Do not promote a box truck to day-cab-truck because the box is tall, the liftgate looks heavy, or the cab is a medium conventional. Day-cab-truck requires a tractor / fifth-wheel layout, not a van body. Rule 6 (CLOSE-UPS -- TYPE ONLY FROM TYPE-SPECIFIC PARTS): a sleeper bunk/cabinet close-up is sleeper-truck. A dump bed, tailgate, or hoist-with-bed close-up is dump-truck. A fifth-wheel or flat day-cab rear-wall close-up is day-cab-truck. Shared parts -- engine bay, analog cluster, one commercial tire, fuel/DEF tank, frame rail, data plate, generic high-mileage LCD -- are NOT a type. Those parts appear on Class 7/8 and on many Class 2–6 trucks. Use none unless the same frame also shows a Rule 1, 2, or 3 layout cue, or an unambiguous Class 7/8 tractor OEM in a tractor-cab context (Freightliner Cascadia / Peterbilt / Kenworth / Mack / Volvo / Western Star / International LT or ProStar grille, hood, or steering-wheel cap -- not a Freightliner M2 oval and not a generic 'International' medium hood). High mileage alone, a silicone charge-air coupler alone, or a fuel tank with diamond-plate steps alone is none. Rule 7 (PRIMARY SUBJECT ONLY): judge the vehicle or part the frame is composed around. Background trucks do not change the label. Rule 8 (WHEN UNCERTAIN): if a dump body is visible, dump-truck. If a sleeper box or bunk is visible, sleeper-truck. If a day-cab tractor / fifth-wheel layout is visible, day-cab-truck. If none of those layouts is visible, use none. Do not default leftover Class 7/8-looking hardware to day-cab-truck.

reasoning.description: Step-by-step visual analysis written BEFORE the final decision. Name the primary subject. Say whether a dump body, a sleeper box/bunk, or a day-cab tractor / fifth-wheel layout is actually visible. Then pick truck_type from that layout, or none if no layout is visible. Do not skip this field.

output.description: Final type decision. day-cab-truck, dump-truck, and sleeper-truck are valid input. none is invalid input.

truck_type.description: Exactly one value, chosen from BODY/CAB LAYOUT. day-cab-truck: Class 7/8 highway tractor whose cab ends at a flat rear wall behind the seats, with open frame to a fifth-wheel and no sleeper box and no dump bed -- or a crop that still shows that tractor-cab / fifth-wheel layout. dump-truck: Class 7/8 truck whose cargo body is an open-top dump, hopper, or grain box (ribbed dump sides, swinging/high-lift tailgate, hoist with the bed, tarp roller, or a view from inside the dump bed). sleeper-truck: Class 7/8 highway tractor with a sleeper box on the exterior (raised/extended compartment, sleeper side window, roof fairing) or a sleeper-compartment interior (bunk mattress, overhead cabinet, netted shelf, sleeper curtain). none: pickups and Super Duty chassis-cabs; cargo vans; step vans; cutaway cubes; enclosed moving/cargo straight box trucks and liftgate-only box rears; medium conventionals with a box (M2, International 4000/MV, F-650/F-750); medium stake/flatbed; service bodies on a pickup; cargo-box interiors; GVWR printed under 26,001 lb; non-trucks; OR a shared-part close-up (engine, dash, one wheel, tank, frame) that does not show a day-cab, dump, or sleeper layout.

user_message.description: When truck_type is day-cab-truck, dump-truck, or sleeper-truck, this MUST be an empty string. When truck_type is none, this MUST be a short message telling the user the photo is not a Class 7/8 day-cab, dump, or sleeper truck and asking them to upload one.
